top_story: An Israeli strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis overnight on 12 November killed six people, including a surgeon, and wounded 28 at one of Gaza’s few functioning medical facilities, deepening the collapse of civilian and medical protection in the territory. The attack hit rooms where doctors were working and sleeping, underscoring how Israel’s military campaign is eroding the infrastructure that sustains daily survival as much as it is targeting militants. Hours later in London, the conviction of two men for surveilling UK-based journalists as part of an Iranian-directed plot, followed by renewed attention to death-row prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani in Iran, highlighted a parallel pattern of coercion that reaches from domestic repression to operations against dissidents abroad. Together, the developments point to a regional climate in which state violence and intimidation are increasingly normalized across borders, with civilians, medical workers, and exiled critics bearing the cost.
